title: Decide which page blocks belong to the main document
description: Choose a page shape and an evidence policy. The workbench classifies every block, then compares the kept set with the editorial target so false inclusions and missing content stay visible.

policies.label: Semantic structure
policies.detail: Keep blocks marked as article or main content. Fast and legible, but only as reliable as the page markup.

policies.label: Text-density gate
policies.detail: Keep long, sentence-rich blocks with at most 35% linked text. Useful when structural markup is weak.

policies.label: Hybrid block score
policies.detail: Combine structure, text length, sentences, repeated-template evidence, and link density in one inspectable score.

scenarios.label: News story
scenarios.detail: One article is surrounded by navigation, related links, and a long discussion thread.
scenarios.target: Keep the headline and article body; exclude site navigation, recommendations, and comments.

blocks.label: Global navigation
blocks.summary: A compact set of section links repeated on every story.

blocks.label: Story headline and byline
blocks.summary: Short but essential article identity and author context.

blocks.label: Story body
blocks.summary: Long prose with paragraphs, quotations, and a small number of citations.

blocks.label: Related stories rail
blocks.summary: Teasers and links selected by the publishing template.

blocks.label: Reader comments
blocks.summary: Substantial prose that resembles article text but is outside the extraction target.

scenarios.label: Product guide
scenarios.detail: Useful prose and specifications share the page with commerce and recommendation modules.
scenarios.target: Keep the product explanation, specification table, and FAQ; exclude purchase chrome and recommendations.

blocks.label: Purchase panel
blocks.summary: Price, delivery, account, and cart controls reused by the storefront.

blocks.label: Product explanation
blocks.summary: The main prose describing capabilities, limits, and intended use.

blocks.label: Specification table
blocks.summary: High-value structured facts with almost no sentence punctuation.

blocks.label: FAQ answers
blocks.summary: Useful answer text inside generic accordion containers.

blocks.label: Recommendation carousel
blocks.summary: Verbose product teasers that can pass a simple density rule.

scenarios.label: Discussion thread
scenarios.detail: The content target spans generic containers rather than one article element.
scenarios.target: Keep the opening question and substantive answers; exclude navigation, signatures, and topic suggestions.

blocks.label: Topic navigation
blocks.summary: Category and breadcrumb links repeated throughout the forum.

blocks.label: Opening question
blocks.summary: The problem statement that gives every answer its context.

blocks.label: Accepted answer
blocks.summary: Substantive prose and code living in an ordinary post container.

blocks.label: Second answer
blocks.summary: A shorter independent answer that still belongs to the document.

blocks.label: User signatures
blocks.summary: Profile slogans and links repeated under many posts.

blocks.label: Suggested topics
blocks.summary: A dense list of neighboring discussions, not part of this thread.
